items.question: Why does DeepWalk rely on restarts in its random walks to improve performance, and how does that teleport probability change the learned embeddings?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk uses restarts/teleport probability as a core mechanism and benefits from them.
items.correction: DeepWalk's random walks could have restarts, but the authors report no advantage from using restarts in their preliminary results.
items.evidence_quote: These walks could have restarts (i.e. a teleport probability of returning back to their root), but our preliminary results did not show any advantage of using restarts.

items.question: What vocabulary does DeepWalk build from the corpus, and how does it treat the graph vertices as a separate vocabulary during training?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk uses the corpus vocabulary and graph vertices as separate vocabularies.
items.correction: DeepWalk treats the graph vertices as its own vocabulary, with V = V.
items.evidence_quote: DeepWalkconsiders a set of short truncated random walks its own corpus, and the graph vertices as its own vocabulary (V =V ).

items.question: Under which conditions does DeepWalk require knowing the vertex frequency distribution ahead of training in order to work correctly?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk requires the vertex frequency distribution ahead of training to function.
items.correction: Knowing the vertex frequency distribution ahead of training is beneficial but not necessary for DeepWalk to work.
items.evidence_quote: While it is beneficial to know the V and the frequency distribution of vertices in the random walks ahead of the training, it is not necessary for the algorithm to work as we will show in 4.2.2.

items.question: How does DeepWalk's update procedure use the CBOW objective to predict a vertex from its neighbors, and why is that better than SkipGram here?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk uses CBOW rather than SkipGram for its update procedure.
items.correction: DeepWalk uses the SkipGram algorithm to update the representations, not CBOW.
items.evidence_quote: We use the SkipGram algorithm [26] to update these representations in accordance with our objective function in Eq. 2.
